characterList.description: A man with long dark hair, glasses, wearing a gray t-shirt. He is seated at a table with a laptop and microphone in front of him.
characterList.name: Ethan Zuckerman

content_metadata.description: A conference session focused on exploring the community dimension of media, featuring a detailed presentation by Ethan Zuckerman on the evolution of digital communities.

qAndA.question: What was the name of the software developed by the BBN team that was essentially the first internet router?
In what year was the first bulletin board system (BBS) created, and what was its name?
What was the French online service that introduced a chess program with a chat feature, leading to the early use of online chat for flirting?
What type of online platform did Ward Cunningham develop in 1995, allowing for collaborative editing of web pages?

qAndA.answer: The introduction of the World Wide Web.
qAndA.question: What significant event in 1990 led to a broader adoption of the internet by a more diverse audience?

narrativeProgression.description: Ethan Zuckerman provides a historical overview of digital communities, starting from the earliest forms of computer communication to the emergence of social media platforms.

scenes.title: The History of Digital Communities

Slideshow with images and text accompanying Ethan Zuckerman's speech.

climax.description: The climax occurs when Zuckerman highlights the significant financial investments in MySpace, marking the mainstream adoption of digital communities.

storylines.description: The video explores the development and implications of digital communities, covering the history and key technological advancements that have led to current social media platforms.
